source.title: A predicted distribution for Galois groups of maximal unramified extensions
source.authors: Yuan Liu, Melanie Matchett Wood and David Zureick-Brown
readSections: arXiv v2 (21 July 2022, 58 pages; e-print SHA-256 4772603bc93a83b2cb6241a7d2896ef044ab7dae9fe333f384fee08a067f79d4, PDF SHA-256 7f1e85da49b23f80fc7abe9a68dbc5384ab216dfa5d55cd5e3223ba3268abed9), read in full from its TeX source on 2026-09-22: Part I §§2–7 and Part II §§8–12. Locators are v2 statement numbers and pages.

The published article is paywalled and was not read; its Publisher Correction (SHA-256 553910550d1a9ae992e4842af9c694735e42fe64190cca755eb95f62b5eddd43) only restyles references. Any change between v2 and the published text is therefore unchecked.

Checked in detail: Proposition 2.2, the embedding argument of Lemma 2.7, Lemmas 3.4–3.6 and Corollaries 3.8–3.10, Proposition 3.13, Lemma 3.17 and Proposition 3.22, the probability formula of Proposition 4.3 and Theorem 4.12, Lemma 5.10 and Theorem 5.12, the moment computation of Theorem 6.2, §7.1, Lemma 9.3, the trace-formula assembly of Theorem 1.4, Proposition 12.7, Lemma 12.10 and the comparison b(G,c,q,n) = b(Γ,Γ∖1,q,n). Liu–Wood 2020, Wood 2021 and Wewers were used as quoted.

summary: Liu, Wood and Zureick-Brown build a random-group model for Gal(K^#/K), the Galois group of the maximal unramified, split-at-∞, prime-to-(roots of unity·|Γ|) extension of a totally real Γ-extension K of Q or F_q(t). They prove two structural facts: Gal(K^#/K) is an admissible Γ-group (Proposition 2.2) and has Property E, lifting along non-split central Z/p extensions (Theorem 2.5, via embedding problems). They define the free admissible Γ-group 𝓕_n and random quotients 𝓕_n/[Y(S)] by n+1 Haar-random relations, which is exactly the class of Property-E quotients (Proposition 3.13). As n → ∞ these converge to a probability measure μ_Γ with explicit values on basic opens (Theorem 1.2, via Theorem 4.12, chief factor pairs and Theorem 5.12). Its moments are E|Sur_Γ(X, H)| = [H : H^Γ]^{−1} (Theorem 6.2), and it abelianizes to Cohen–Lenstra–Martinet and pro-p-completes to Boston–Bush–Hajir (§7). They conjecture that Gal(K^#/K) is μ_Γ-distributed (Conjecture 1.3) and prove every moment in the q → ∞ function-field limit (Theorem 1.4; Corollary 1.5 for class groups). The proof counts Frobenius-fixed components of Hurwitz schemes with the Ellenberg–Venkatesh–Westerland/Wood lifting invariant (Theorem 10.4, §§10–12). The atlas has free profinite groups (ProfiniteProPGroups), the point-count trace formula and weight bounds (SF.2, EDC.2, DWP.7), Hurwitz schemes and embedding problems (IG.4–IG.5), function-field statistics (ST.5) and, via PAPER-WOOD-19, a proposed reduced-Schur Part II. It has nothing on random Γ-groups. The random-group theory (§§1–7) becomes a new Part II of Arithmetic statistics. The Galois facts go to IG.4, the Hurwitz and component machinery to IG.5 (stable braid orbits to IG.3), the reduced-multiplier group theory to the WOOD-19 candidate, the function-field moment theorem to ST.5, and a lattice-point lemma to GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.4. Four source issues are recorded, all in arXiv v2 (the published text could not be read): a wrong equation reference in the proof of Theorem 4.12, 'N(E, …)' for N(H, …) in the proof of Theorem 1.4, (Z_p[Γ])^n for the augmentation-ideal lattice in §7.1, and Theorem 5.12 stated only for u ≥ 0 while later results use every integer u.

items.name: Admissible Γ-groups, level-𝒞 completions and the space 𝒫
items.statement: Γ is a finite group; a Γ-group is a profinite group with a continuous Γ-action; Sur_Γ, Hom_Γ, Aut_Γ are Γ-equivariant maps; for a generating set γ_1, …, γ_d of Γ, Y : G → G^d, g ↦ (g^{−1}γ_1(g), …, g^{−1}γ_d(g)). G is admissible if it is topologically generated by {g^{−1}γ(g) : g ∈ G, γ ∈ Γ} and has order (supernatural) prime to |Γ|. For a set 𝒞 of finite Γ-groups, 𝒞̄ is its closure under finite products, Γ-subgroups and Γ-quotients, and G^𝒞 = lim G/M over closed normal Γ-subgroups with G/M ∈ 𝒞̄ (a functor to level-𝒞 groups preserving surjections). 𝒫 is the set of isomorphism classes of admissible |Γ|′-Γ-groups with all G^𝒞 finite, topologized by the basic opens U_{𝒞,H} = {X : X^𝒞 ≅ H}. A finite abelian |Γ|′-Γ-group is admissible iff H^Γ = 1 (§7.1).
items.note: The basic notions of the random-group theory.

items.name: Theorem 1.2: the limiting distribution μ_Γ
items.statement: For every finite group Γ there is a probability measure μ_Γ on the set of isomorphism classes of admissible Γ-groups (on 𝒫) such that, as n → ∞, the distributions of X_{Γ,n} = 𝓕_n/[Y(S)] (S = n+1 Haar-random elements of the free admissible Γ-group 𝓕_n) converge weakly to μ_Γ. Explicitly (5.13), μ_Γ(U_{𝒞,H}) = |Aut_Γ(H)|^{−1}[H : H^Γ]^{−1} ∏_{G∈𝒜_H} ∏_{i≥1}(1 − λ(𝒞,H,G) h_{H⋊Γ}(G)^{−i}/[G : G^Γ]) ∏_{G∈𝒩} e^{−λ(𝒞,H,G)/[G:G^Γ]}.
items.locator: Theorem 1.2, p. 2 (arXiv v2), proof in §5.3, p. 30
items.note: μ_Γ = μ_1. Weak convergence via Carathéodory extension (Theorem 5.12) and Fatou's lemma on open sets.

items.name: Conjecture 1.3: Gal(K^#/K) is distributed according to μ_Γ
items.statement: Q is Q or F_q(t); b = 2|Γ| for Q = Q and q(q−1)|Γ| for F_q(t); for a Γ-extension K/Q, K^# is the maximal extension of K unramified everywhere, split completely above ∞, with all finite subextensions of degree prime to b. Let q be prime to |Γ|, 𝒞 a finite set of finite Γ-groups of order prime to b and H a finite admissible such group. With E_Γ(D, Q) the totally real Γ-extensions with radical discriminant norm rD(K) = D: lim_B Σ_{D≤B} #{K ∈ E_Γ(D,Q) : Gal(K^#/K)^𝒞 ≅ H^𝒞} / Σ_{D≤B} |E_Γ(D,Q)| = μ_Γ(U_{𝒞,H}), and lim_B Σ_{D≤B} Σ_K |Sur_Γ(Gal(K^#/K), H)| / Σ_{D≤B} |E_Γ(D,Q)| = ∫ |Sur_Γ(X, H)| dμ_Γ = [H : H^Γ]^{−1}.
items.locator: Conjecture 1.3, p. 3 (arXiv v2)
items.note: A conjecture, recorded as a statement. It implies the Cohen–Martinet predictions (prime-to-|Γ| parts, fields ordered by radical discriminant) and the Boston–Bush–Hajir predictions for real quadratic fields.

items.name: Theorem 1.4: function-field moments as q → ∞
items.statement: Let Γ be finite and H a finite admissible Γ-group. Then lim_{b→∞} lim_{q→∞, (q,|Γ||H|)=1, (q−1,|H|)=1} Σ_{n≤b} Σ_{K∈E_Γ(q^n,F_q(t))} |Sur_Γ(Gal(K^#/K), H)| / Σ_{n≤b} |E_Γ(q^n,F_q(t))| = ∫ |Sur_Γ(X,H)| dμ_Γ(X) = [H : H^Γ]^{−1}, q running over prime powers.
items.locator: Theorem 1.4, p. 2 (arXiv v2), proof in §10.2, pp. 40–41
items.note: Proof: Lemma 9.3 (count of surjections), Lemma 10.2 (F_q-points of Hurwitz schemes), Lemma 10.3 with Grothendieck–Lefschetz and Deligne's bound, Theorem 10.4 (Frobenius-fixed components), and Theorem 6.2 (u = 1).

items.name: Corollary 1.5: Cohen–Lenstra–Martinet moments over F_q(t)
items.statement: Let H be a finite abelian Γ-group with (|H|, |Γ|) = 1 and H^Γ = 1. Then lim_{b} lim_{q→∞, (q,|Γ||H|)=1, (q−1,|H|)=1} Σ_{n≤b} Σ_{K∈E_Γ(q^n,F_q(t))} |Sur_Γ(Cl(O_K), H)| / Σ_{n≤b} |E_Γ(q^n,F_q(t))| = |H|^{−1}.
items.locator: Corollary 1.5, p. 4 (arXiv v2)
items.note: Gal(K^#/K)^ab is the prime-to-q(q−1)|Γ| part of Cl(O_K) by class field theory. These are the Cohen–Lenstra/Cohen–Martinet averages, with fields ordered by radical discriminant; by Wang–Wood the moments determine the distribution.

items.name: Definition 2.1: the Γ-action on Gal(K^#/K)
items.statement: Q is Q or F_q(t); b = 2|Γ| for Q = Q and q(q−1)|Γ| for F_q(t); for a Γ-extension K/Q, K^# is the maximal extension of K unramified everywhere, split completely above ∞, with all finite subextensions of degree prime to b. For a pro-|Γ|′ extension L/K Galois over Q, a section s : Γ → Gal(L/Q) (Schur–Zassenhaus) gives Gal(L/Q) ≅ Gal(L/K) ⋊ Γ and a Γ-action on Gal(L/K), well defined up to isomorphism because all sections are conjugate. Definition 2.1 fixes such a section for K^#.
items.locator: Definition 2.1, p. 10 (arXiv v2), and the preceding paragraph, p. 10
items.note: Conjugacy of all complements in the coprime case is the Schur–Zassenhaus theorem; in general its proof uses Feit–Thompson (see the Schur–Zassenhaus item).

items.name: Proposition 2.2: unramified Galois groups are admissible
items.statement: Let K be a Γ-extension of Q and L an unramified pro-|Γ|′ extension of K, Galois over Q and split completely above ∞. Then Gal(L/K) is an admissible Γ-group.
items.locator: Proposition 2.2, p. 10 (arXiv v2)
items.note: The Γ-coinvariant quotient Ḡ gives an unramified Ḡ-extension of Q split at ∞, hence trivial (Minkowski for Q; for F_q(t), the absence of such extensions). PAPER-WOOD-19 routes the same 'no unramified split-infinity extension of the base' input to IG.4.

items.name: Definition 2.3: Property E
items.statement: For a full subcategory C of Γ-groups, H ∈ C has Property E if for every non-split central extension 1 → Z/pZ → G̃ → G → 1 in C (p prime, trivial Γ-action on Z/pZ), every Γ-surjection H → G lifts to a Γ-surjection H → G̃.
items.locator: Definition 2.3, p. 11 (arXiv v2)
items.note: Group-theoretic; the random-group Part II owns it.

items.name: Theorem 2.5 with Lemmas 2.6–2.7: Gal(K^#/K) has Property E
items.statement: Q is Q or F_q(t); b = 2|Γ| for Q = Q and q(q−1)|Γ| for F_q(t); for a Γ-extension K/Q, K^# is the maximal extension of K unramified everywhere, split completely above ∞, with all finite subextensions of degree prime to b. For every Γ-extension K/Q, Gal(K^#/K) has Property E in the category of b′-Γ-groups. Lemma 2.6: for p prime to the order of the roots of unity in Q, local characters φ_v : Gal_{Q_v} → Z/p (almost all unramified) come from a global φ agreeing with φ_v on inertia at finite v and on Gal_{Q_∞}. Lemma 2.7: for G a |Γ|′-Γ-group, L/Q a (G⋊Γ)-extension with L/L^G unramified and split at ∞, p ∤ b, and a non-split central Γ-extension 1 → Z/p → G̃ → G → 1, there is L̃ ⊃ L with Gal(L̃/Q) ≅ G̃ ⋊ Γ compatibly, L̃/L^G unramified and split at ∞.
items.locator: Theorem 2.5, p. 11 (arXiv v2), Lemmas 2.6–2.7, pp. 11–12
items.note: An embedding-problem argument: local solutions with trivial inertia on N, the local–global principle for central embedding problems (Malle–Matzat Cor. 10.2), correction by a global character (Lemma 2.6; Serre, Topics, 2.1.6), and an inverse limit for profinite G.

items.name: Schur–Zassenhaus for profinite groups
items.statement: If K is a closed normal subgroup of a profinite group G with (#K, #G/K) = 1, then K has a complement, and all complements are conjugate (Ribes–Zalesskii, Theorem 2.3.15). Consequently, for H a finite |Γ|′-Γ-group, the sections of H⋊Γ → Γ form a single H-conjugacy orbit with stabilizer H^Γ, so there are [H : H^Γ] of them (used in Lemmas 3.4 and 9.3).
items.locator: §2, p. 10; proofs of Lemmas 3.4, 3.6, 5.2, 9.3 and Theorem 10.4 (Ribes–Zalesskii 2.3.15)
items.note: Mathlib proves existence for finite groups (Subgroup.exists_right_complement'_of_coprime) but not the conjugacy statement, whose general proof uses the Feit–Thompson theorem (one of the two coprime orders is odd) or a solvability hypothesis. Theorem 1.4's exact constant depends on it through Lemma 9.3. Owned by the random-group Part II, which needs it throughout.

items.name: The free admissible Γ-group 𝓕_n and Lemma 3.1
items.statement: Γ is a finite group; a Γ-group is a profinite group with a continuous Γ-action; Sur_Γ, Hom_Γ, Aut_Γ are Γ-equivariant maps; for a generating set γ_1, …, γ_d of Γ, Y : G → G^d, g ↦ (g^{−1}γ_1(g), …, g^{−1}γ_d(g)). F_n(Γ) is the free pro-|Γ|′ group on {x_{i,γ} : 1 ≤ i ≤ n, γ ∈ Γ} with σ(x_{i,γ}) = x_{i,σγ}; 𝓕_n(Γ) is the closed Γ-subgroup generated by x_i^{−1}γ_j(x_i), x_i = x_{i,1}. Lemma 3.1: 𝓕_n is admissible, and there is a Γ-quotient map π : F_n → 𝓕_n with π ∘ (inclusion) = id. Remark 3.2: as a pro-|Γ|′ group 𝓕_n is free on {x_i^{−1}σ(x_i) : σ ≠ 1}; it is Γ-generated by n elements; and any H Γ-generated by elements h_i^{−1}γ(h_i) is a quotient of 𝓕_n.
items.locator: Lemma 3.1, p. 13 (arXiv v2), §3.1 and Remark 3.2, p. 13
items.note: Free pro-|Γ|′ groups on finite sets come from ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 4 (the planned item below).

items.name: Lemmas 3.4–3.6: the map Y and sections
items.statement: Γ is a finite group; a Γ-group is a profinite group with a continuous Γ-action; Sur_Γ, Hom_Γ, Aut_Γ are Γ-equivariant maps; for a generating set γ_1, …, γ_d of Γ, Y : G → G^d, g ↦ (g^{−1}γ_1(g), …, g^{−1}γ_d(g)). Y(G) is in bijection with the sections of G⋊Γ → Γ. Lemma 3.4: for a |Γ|′-Γ-group G and Γ-subgroup E, Y(E) = Y(G) ∩ E^d. Lemma 3.5: for finite G, Y^{−1}(Y(g)) = G^Γ g, so |G| = |G^Γ||Y(G)|. Lemma 3.6: for 1 → N → G → H → 1 of finite |Γ|′-Γ-groups, 1 → N^Γ → G^Γ → H^Γ → 1 is exact, |Y(N)| = |Y(G)|/|Y(H)|, and |Y(G) ∩ π^{−1}(x)| = |Y(G)|/|Y(H)| for x ∈ Y(H).
items.locator: Lemma 3.4, p. 14 (arXiv v2), Lemmas 3.5–3.6, pp. 14–15
items.note: H¹(Γ, N) = 0 by Schur–Zassenhaus.

items.name: Corollary 3.8, Lemma 3.9 and Corollary 3.10: homomorphisms from 𝓕_n
items.statement: For any Γ-group G, Y(G)^n → Hom_Γ(𝓕_n, G), (Y(g_i)) ↦ (x_i ↦ g_i)|_{𝓕_n}, is a bijection (Corollary 3.8). An admissible G is Γ-generated by the coordinates of Y(G), so 𝓕_n is independent of the generating set of Γ (Lemma 3.9). 𝓕_n^{ab} ≅ (Z[Γ]/(Σ_g g))^n with Z = ∏_{p∤|Γ|} Z_p, and (𝓕_n^{ab})^Γ = 1 (Corollary 3.10).
items.locator: Corollary 3.8, p. 14 (arXiv v2), Lemma 3.9 and Corollary 3.10, pp. 14–15

items.name: Proposition 3.13 (with Lemma 3.12): Property E ⟺ relations of the form Y(r)
items.statement: Lemma 3.12: if G̃ is admissible and N a normal Γ-subgroup with trivial Γ-action, then G̃ acts trivially on N. Proposition 3.13: for a set 𝒞 of finite |Γ|′-Γ-groups and a Γ-surjection φ : (𝓕_n)^𝒞 → H, ker φ = [Y(ker φ)] iff H has Property E in the category of level-𝒞 Γ-groups.
items.locator: Proposition 3.13, p. 16 (arXiv v2), with Lemma 3.12, pp. 15–16
items.note: The motivation for taking relations Y(r).

items.name: Definition 3.15: the random groups X_{Γ,n,u} and the measures μ_{u,n}, μ_u
items.statement: For n ≥ 1 and u > −n, X_{Γ,n,u} = 𝓕_n/[Y(S)] with S a multiset of n+u independent Haar-random elements of 𝓕_n (u = 1 by default); μ_{n,u}(A) = Prob(X_{u,n} ∈ A) on Borel subsets of 𝒫, and μ_u(A) = lim_n μ_{n,u}(A) on the algebra generated by the basic opens (3.16). For finite 𝒞, (𝓕_n)^𝒞 is finite.
items.locator: Definition 3.15, p. 17 (arXiv v2), and (3.16), p. 17
items.note: Haar measure on the compact group 𝓕_n is in Mathlib (MeasureTheory.Measure.haar); the pro-𝒞 finiteness argument is the paper's.

items.name: Proposition 3.22 (with Lemma 3.17): p-class tower groups occur in the model
items.statement: Q is Q or F_q(t); b = 2|Γ| for Q = Q and q(q−1)|Γ| for F_q(t); for a Γ-extension K/Q, K^# is the maximal extension of K unramified everywhere, split completely above ∞, with all finite subextensions of degree prime to b. Let p ∤ b with μ_p ⊄ K, and let G_{K,p} be the maximal pro-p quotient of Gal(K^#/K). Lemma 3.17: in the notation of §3.3 there is an F_p[Γ]-surjection F_p[Γ]^{n+1} → N/N* (via Hochschild–Serre, Koch Theorem 11.3 and O_K^×/p ↪ F_p[Γ]/(Σ g)). Proposition 3.22: if G_{K,p} = [Y({h_1,…,h_n})], then G_{K,p} ≅ (𝓕_n)_p/[Y(S)] for some S ⊂ (𝓕_n)_p with |S| = n+1.
items.locator: Proposition 3.22, p. 19 (arXiv v2), with Lemma 3.17, pp. 18–20
items.note: Uses the finite presentation of G_{K,p} (Koch, Chapter 11) and pro-p generation theory (NSW Corollary 3.9.3).

items.name: The fundamental short exact sequence and the multiplicities m(𝒞, n, H, G)
items.statement: For finite 𝒞, a Γ-surjection ϖ : (𝓕_n)^𝒞 → H with kernel N, and M the intersection of the maximal proper (𝓕_n)^𝒞-normal Γ-subgroups of N: 1 → R → F → H → 1 with F = (𝓕_n)^𝒞/M, R = N/M (4.1), induced by 1 → R → F⋊Γ → H⋊Γ → 1 (4.2); R is a product of irreducible F⋊Γ-groups. 𝒜_H is the set of non-trivial finite abelian irreducible |Γ|′-(H⋊Γ)-groups and 𝒩 the set of finite |Γ|′-Γ-groups isomorphic to T^j (T non-abelian simple); m(𝒞, n, H, G) is the multiplicity of G in R (summed over the compatible F⋊Γ-structures for G ∈ 𝒩), independent of ϖ (Remark 4.9).

items.name: Proposition 4.3 and Remark 4.4: probability that Y-relations generate R
items.statement: For a Γ-group F and R = ∏ G_i^{m_i} with pairwise non-isomorphic finite irreducible F⋊Γ-groups G_i, and n+u ≥ 1 uniform random r_1, …, r_{n+u} ∈ R: Prob([Y({r_j})]_{F⋊Γ} = R) = ∏_{G_i abelian} ∏_{j=0}^{m_i−1}(1 − h_{F⋊Γ}(G_i)^j |Y(G_i)|^{−n−u}) ∏_{G_i non-abelian}(1 − |Y(G_i)|^{−n−u})^{m_i}, where h_G(H) = |Hom_G(H, H)|. Remark 4.4: for G abelian irreducible, h_{F⋊Γ}(G)^𝔪 = |Y(G)| with 𝔪 maximal such that G^𝔪 is generated by the coordinates of one Y(g).
items.locator: Proposition 4.3, p. 21 (arXiv v2), and Remark 4.4, p. 21
items.note: Uses Liu–Wood's Lemmas 5.5 and 5.8.

items.name: Lemma 4.6, Proposition 4.7 and Corollary 4.8: counting H-extensions
items.statement: Lemma 4.6: for ρ : (𝓕_n)^𝒞 → H and an H-extension (E, π), |Sur_{Γ,H}(ρ, π)| = Σ_{D∈𝓔^E_H} ν(D, E)(|Y(D)|/|Y(H)|)^n if E is admissible of level 𝒞, and 0 otherwise (ν the Möbius function of the poset of sub-H-extensions). Proposition 4.7 counts |Sur_{F⋊Γ}(R, G)| over the admissible level-𝒞 H-extensions 𝓔_𝒞(G, H) with kernel G. Corollary 4.8: for G ∈ 𝒜_H, (h_{H⋊Γ}(G)^m − 1)/(h_{H⋊Γ}(G) − 1) = Σ_{(E,π)∈𝓔_𝒞(G,H)} Σ_D ν(D,E)(|Y(D)|/|Y(H)|)^n / |Aut_{Γ,H}(E,π)|, and for G ∈ 𝒩, m equals the same sum.
items.locator: Lemma 4.6, p. 22 (arXiv v2), Proposition 4.7 and Corollary 4.8, pp. 22–23
items.note: Uses Liu–Wood's Theorem 7.1 and Proposition 8.7.

items.name: Theorem 4.12: the measures of basic opens and their limits
items.statement: Let 𝒞 be a finite set of finite |Γ|′-Γ-groups and H a finite admissible level-𝒞 Γ-group; n ≥ 1, u > −n. Then Prob((X_{u,n})^𝒞 ≅ H) = |Sur_Γ(𝓕_n, H)| / (|Aut_Γ(H)||Y(H)|^{n+u}) · ∏_{G∈𝒜_H} ∏_{k=0}^{m−1}(1 − h_{H⋊Γ}(G)^k/|Y(G)|^{n+u}) ∏_{G∈𝒩}(1 − |Y(G)|^{−n−u})^m (m = m(𝒞,n,H,G)), and lim_n equals |Aut_Γ(H)|^{−1}|Y(H)|^{−u} ∏_{G∈𝒜_H} ∏_{i≥1}(1 − λ(𝒞,H,G) h_{H⋊Γ}(G)^{−i}/|Y(G)|^u) ∏_{G∈𝒩} e^{−|Y(G)|^{−u}λ(𝒞,H,G)}, with λ as in (4.10)–(4.11); only finitely many factors are non-trivial.
items.locator: Theorem 4.12, p. 24 (arXiv v2), with (4.10)–(4.11); proof as corrected by E1
items.note: Uses Liu–Wood's Corollary 6.12, Lemma 6.1 and Lemma 8.11. The proof cites the fundamental sequence as (7.1); it is (4.1) (E1).

items.name: Definition 5.1, Lemma 5.2 and Corollary 5.3: Γ-chief factor pairs
items.statement: For a finite |Γ|′-Γ-group G, CF_Γ(G) is the set of isomorphism classes of chief factor pairs (M, A) ∈ CF(G⋊Γ) with gcd(|M|, |Γ|) = 1, and CF_Γ(𝒞) = ∪_{G∈𝒞} CF_Γ(G). Lemma 5.2: if 𝒞 is closed under Γ-subgroups and Γ-quotients then CF_Γ(𝒞̄) = CF_Γ(𝒞). Corollary 5.3: if all groups in 𝒞 have order ≤ ℓ, then for (M, A) ∈ CF_Γ(𝒞̄) the prime-to-|Γ| part of |A/Inn(M)| is < ℓ, and CF_Γ(𝒞̄) is finite.
items.locator: Definition 5.1, p. 26 (arXiv v2), Lemma 5.2 and Corollary 5.3, pp. 26–27
items.note: Extends Liu–Wood's chief factor pairs (Lemmas 6.3, 6.11 and 6.13) to Γ-groups.

items.name: Lemma 5.4 and Corollary 5.9: multiplicity bounds at level ℓ
items.statement: For H of level 𝒞_ℓ (all Γ-groups of order ≤ ℓ) and H̃ = H^{𝒞_{ℓ−1}}: the number of G ∈ 𝒜_H isomorphic to a given abelian M with some m(𝒞_ℓ, n, H, G) ≠ 0 is at most Σ_{(M,A)∈CF_Γ(𝒞̄_ℓ)} |Sur(H̃⋊Γ, A)|, and the number of level-𝒞_ℓ H-extensions with non-abelian irreducible kernel M is at most Σ |Sur(H̃⋊Γ, A/Inn(M))| (Lemma 5.4). Hence there is c(u, ℓ, H̃) > 0 with P_{u,n}(U_{𝒞_ℓ,H}) = 0 or ≥ c(u, ℓ, H̃) for all H over H̃ (Corollary 5.9).
items.locator: Lemma 5.4, p. 27 (arXiv v2), and Corollary 5.9, pp. 27–28
items.note: Corollary 5.9 follows Liu–Wood Lemma 9.5.

items.name: Lemma 5.10: interchanging limits and sums over the level tower
items.statement: Let f_n(H, ℓ) ≥ 0 be defined for finite Γ-groups H of level 𝒞_ℓ with f_n = g_n · P_{u,n}(U_{𝒞_ℓ,H}), g_n → g monotonically from below, and Σ_{H over H̃} f_n(H, ℓ) = f_n(H̃, ℓ−1). Then lim_n f_n(H, ℓ) exists and Σ_H lim_n f_n(H, ℓ) = lim_n f_n(1, 1).
items.locator: Lemma 5.10, p. 29 (arXiv v2)
items.note: By induction on ℓ and dominated convergence, using Corollary 5.9.

items.name: Theorem 5.12: countable additivity of μ_u
items.statement: For every integer u, μ_u is countably additive on the algebra generated by the basic opens U_{𝒞,H}, hence extends uniquely to a Borel probability measure on 𝒫.
items.locator: Theorem 5.12, p. 30 (arXiv v2), statement as corrected by E4
items.note: Printed for u ≥ 0 only, although Theorems 5.15, 6.2 and 7.4 use μ_u for all u. The proof (Lemma 5.10 with f_n = μ_{u,n}(U_{𝒞_ℓ,H})) never uses u ≥ 0 (E4).

items.name: Definition 5.14 and Theorem 5.15: μ_u on V_{𝒞,H} for arbitrary 𝒞
items.statement: For any set 𝒞 of finite |Γ|′-Γ-groups, finite admissible H of level 𝒞 and integer u, with m and λ extended to infinite 𝒞 as limits over an exhausting chain 𝒟_1 ⊂ 𝒟_2 ⊂ ⋯ (Definition 5.14): μ_u(V_{𝒞,H}) = μ_u({X : X^𝒞 ≅ H}) = |Aut_Γ(H)|^{−1}|Y(H)|^{−u} ∏_{G∈𝒜_H} ∏_{i≥1}(1 − λ(𝒞,H,G) h_{H⋊Γ}(G)^{−i}/|Y(G)|^u) ∏_{G∈𝒩} e^{−|Y(G)|^{−u}λ(𝒞,H,G)}.
items.locator: Theorem 5.15, p. 31 (arXiv v2), with Definition 5.14, p. 31
items.note: As in Liu–Wood Lemma 11.3.

items.name: Lemma 6.1 and Theorem 6.2: the moments of μ_u
items.statement: For a finite admissible |Γ|′-Γ-group A and any integer u: lim_n E|Sur_Γ(X_{u,n}, A)| = [A : A^Γ]^{−u} (Lemma 6.1), and if X_u has distribution μ_u then E|Sur_Γ(X_u, A)| = [A : A^Γ]^{−u} (Theorem 6.2). In particular the μ_Γ-moment is [A : A^Γ]^{−1}.
items.locator: Theorem 6.2, p. 32 (arXiv v2), with Lemma 6.1, pp. 31–33
items.note: The interchange of limit and sum uses Lemma 5.10 with f_n(H, ℓ) = E(|Sur_Γ(X_{u,n}, A)| · 1_{X^{𝒞_ℓ} ≅ H}). For u = 0 these are Boston–Wood's imaginary-quadratic moments.

items.name: §7.1: abelianization gives the Cohen–Lenstra–Martinet distribution
items.statement: For 𝒞 the abelian |Γ|′-Γ-groups and finite abelian H with H^Γ = 1: m(𝒞, n, H, G) = n𝔪_G and λ(𝒞, H, G) = 1 for G with trivial H-action, and μ_u(V_{𝒞,H}) = |Aut_Γ(H)|^{−1}|H|^{−u} ∏_{p∤|Γ|} ∏_{G nontrivial irreducible F_p[Γ]-rep} ∏_{i≥1}(1 − h_Γ(G)^{−i}/|G|^u). For u = 1 this is the Cohen–Lenstra–Martinet prediction for prime-to-|Γ| class groups of totally real Γ-fields (u = 0, 1 and Γ = Z/2: imaginary/real quadratic).
items.locator: §7.1, pp. 33–34; as corrected by E3
items.note: Uses that finite-index Γ-submodules N_p of (𝓕_n)^𝒞_p ≅ (Z_p[Γ]/(Σ g))^n are isomorphic to it (Z_p[Γ] hereditary; Serre, Linear representations §16 Thm 34). The text writes (Z_p[Γ])^n (E3). Agreement with Cohen–Martinet in Wang–Wood's Proposition 6.5.

items.name: Lemma 7.2 and Theorems 7.4–7.5: Boston–Bush–Hajir distributions
items.statement: Let Γ = Z/2, p odd, 𝒞 the finite p-Γ-groups (or those of p-class ≤ c). For H of the form 𝓕_n^𝒞/[Y(S)] with |S| = n+u: μ_u(V_{𝒞,H}) = |Aut_Γ(H)|^{−1}|Y(H)|^{−u} ∏_{i≥1+u+d(H)−r(H)}(1 − p^{−i}) (Theorem 7.4; d, r the generator and relation ranks), and for p-class c the same with r(H) replaced by r(H) − ν(H) when cl_p(H) = c (ν the nuclear rank) (Theorem 7.5); otherwise μ_u(V_{𝒞,H}) = 0. For u = 0, 1 these are the Boston–Bush–Hajir measures for imaginary and real quadratic fields. Lemma 7.2 identifies the fundamental sequence with the p-covering-group sequence (7.1).
items.locator: Theorem 7.4, p. 35 (arXiv v2), Lemma 7.2, Remark 7.3 and Theorem 7.5, pp. 34–37
items.note: Uses Liu–Wood Lemma 12.5.

items.name: Lemmas 9.1 and 9.3: counting unramified H-extensions via H⋊Γ-extensions
items.statement: Lemma 9.1: for a Γ-group H and profinite G, Sur(G, H⋊Γ) is in bijection with tuples (ρ ∈ Sur(G, Γ), N closed normal ⊂ ker ρ, section s : Γ → G/N, φ ∈ Isom_Γ(ker ρ/N, H)). Lemma 9.3: for H a finite |Γ|′-Γ-group, Σ_{K∈E_Γ(D,Q)} |Sur_Γ(Gal(K^{un,∞}/K), H)| = [H : H^Γ]^{−1} N(H, Γ, D, Q), where N counts surjections Gal(Q̄/Q) → H⋊Γ whose H-extension is unramified and split above ∞, whose Γ-extension is split at ∞, with rD = D.
items.locator: Lemma 9.1, p. 37 (arXiv v2), and Lemma 9.3, pp. 37–38
items.note: The factor [H : H^Γ] is the number of sections (Schur–Zassenhaus conjugacy).

items.name: Hurwitz stacks and schemes: Hur^n_G, Hur^n_{G,1}, Hur^n_{G,*}, 𝓗ur^n_{G,c}
items.statement: Hur^n_G is the stack of tame Galois covers X → P^1_S with n branch points and G ≅ Aut; Theorem 11.1 (Wewers): it is a separated DM stack, smooth of finite type over Z with coarse scheme, and the branch-locus map to Conf^n(P^1) is étale, and proper over Z[1/|G|]. Hur^n_{G,1} adds a point over ∞ (algebraic, separated, with coarse scheme; Lemma 11.2); Hur^n_{G,*} requires that point unramified: it is a scheme, finite étale over Conf^n(A^1)_{Z[1/|G|]} (Proposition 11.4). For G, c as in Notation 10.1 (c a conjugation- and invertible-power-stable generating subset of G∖1), 𝓗ur^n_{G,c} is the union of components of (Hur^n_{G,*})_{Z[1/|G|]} whose inertia groups are generated by elements of c (component-constant by Wood's Theorem 3.1 and Remark 5.3).
items.locator: Theorem 11.1, p. 42 (arXiv v2), Lemma 11.2, Remark 11.3, Proposition 11.4 and §11.4, pp. 41–45
items.note: PAPER-WOOD-19 and PAPER-ELLENBERG-VENKATESH-WESTERLAND-16 route the marked Hurwitz scheme to IG.5.

items.name: Proposition 11.5, Remark 11.6 and Theorem 11.7: analytic and topological Hurwitz spaces
items.statement: Hall's relative GAGA (a morphism of analytic stacks inducing equivalences on local Artinian points is an equivalence) and stacky GAGA give equivalences (Hur^n_G)_an ≃ Hur^{n,an}_G and (Hur^n_{G,*})_an ≃ Hur^{n,an}_{G,*} (Theorem 11.7). Hur^{n,an}_{G,*} is isomorphic to the topological Hurwitz space Hur^{n,top}_{G,*}, a covering space of Conf^n(A^1)(C) (§11.3).
items.locator: Theorem 11.7, p. 44 (arXiv v2), Proposition 11.5, Remark 11.6 and §11.3, pp. 43–45
items.note: Uses Artin's algebraization of formal moduli II (Theorem 7.3) and Knutson.

items.name: Lemma 10.2: F_q-points of 𝓗ur^n_{G,c} count the extensions
items.statement: Let H be a finite |Γ|′-Γ-group, G = H⋊Γ and c the elements of G of the same order as their image in Γ. For q prime to |G| and n ≥ 0, |𝓗ur^n_{G,c}(F_q)| = N(H, Γ, q^n, F_q(t)).
items.locator: Lemma 10.2, p. 39 (arXiv v2), proof p. 45
items.note: Split completely at ∞ forces constant field F_q, so the covers are geometrically connected; rD(K) = q^{deg branch divisor}.

items.name: Lemma 10.3: cohomology comparison for components
items.statement: For a connected component Y of 𝓗ur^n_{G,c}, i ≥ 0, q prime to |G| and primes ℓ ∤ q, ℓ > n: Y_{F̄_q} is smooth of dimension n and dim H^i_{c,ét}(Y_{F̄_q}, Q_ℓ) = dim H^{2n−i}(Y_C, Q).
items.locator: Lemma 10.3, p. 39 (arXiv v2), proof p. 46
items.note: Poincaré duality, EVW Proposition 7.7 (upgraded from Z/ℓ to Q_ℓ coefficients) on the ordered-configuration cover, S_n-invariants, and the Artin comparison.

items.name: Lemma 11.8: Frobenius on Hurwitz points
items.statement: For q prime to |G|, Frob of (𝓗ur^n_{G,c})_{F_q} sends the F̄_q-point (f, ι, P) to its base change (f^F, ι^F, P^F) along F : x ↦ x^q.
items.locator: Lemma 11.8, p. 46 (arXiv v2)

items.name: Reduced multiplier H_2(G, c), the groups U(G, c), K(G, c) and the powering action
items.statement: For G, c as in Notation 10.1: Q_c ⊂ H_2(G, Z) is generated by ⟨x, y⟩ for x ∈ c, y commuting with x; H_2(G, c) = H_2(G, Z)/Q_c; S̄ = S/τ_S(Q_c) for a Schur cover S, with H_2(G, c) ≅ ker(S̄ → G); U(G, c) = S̄ ×_{G^ab} Z^{c/G}; K(G, c) = ker(U(G, c) → G), with [x] = (x̂, e_x). The group Ẑ^× acts on the set K(G, c) by α*(g, m) = (g^α W_α(m), m^α), with W_α(γ) = x̂_γ^{−α} (x_γ^α)^. The sets K(G,c)⟨−1⟩, Z^{c/G}_{≥M}⟨−1⟩ and 𝔖^{c,G} (Ẑ^×-orbits) are as in §12.
items.note: PAPER-WOOD-19 proposes the Part II InductionRestrictionPartIIReducedSchur for exactly these (reduced Schur multiplier, reduced cover, universal marked extension, discrete power action).

items.name: Lemma 12.10: compatible Schur covers for H⋊Γ → Γ
items.statement: Let H be an admissible |Γ|′-Γ-group and G = H⋊Γ. There are Schur covering groups S → G and S_Γ → Γ with S → S_Γ over G → Γ, and ρ : H_2(G, Z) → H_2(Γ, Z) has kernel of order prime to |Γ|.
items.locator: Lemma 12.10, p. 53 (arXiv v2), p. 53
items.note: Splits M = H_2(G) into its |H|- and |Γ|-primary parts.

items.name: Theorem 12.1 and Corollary 12.2: the lifting invariant of components
items.statement: For every algebraically closed k of characteristic prime to |G| and k-point s̄ of 𝓗ur^n_{G,c} there is a lifting invariant 𝔷_s̄ ∈ K(G, c)_{n,≥0}⟨−1⟩_k, compatible with specialization (across fields, via an isomorphism of Ẑ(1)'s; over a fixed k, the identity) and with Frobenius: 𝔷_{Frob(s̄)}(ζ) = q^{−1} * 𝔷_s̄(ζ). Hence points of one component share the lifting invariant, and geometric points of one component of 𝓗ur^n_{G,c} share its image in 𝔖^{c,G} (Corollary 12.2).
items.locator: Theorem 12.1, p. 48 (arXiv v2), and Corollary 12.2, p. 48
items.note: Wood, Res. Math. Sci. 8 (2021), Theorems 5.2, 2.5, 6.1 and §6.1. PAPER-WOOD-19 routes the analogous component invariant and its specialization compatibility to IG.5 (its items /80, /135).

items.name: Theorem 12.4 and Corollary 12.6: complex components as braid orbits, labelled by lifting invariants
items.statement: Over C, with standard generators γ_i of π_1(P^1 ∖ {P_i}, ∞), the fiber of 𝓗ur^n_{G,c} over P is {(g_1,…,g_n) ∈ c^n : g_1⋯g_n = 1, ⟨g_i⟩ = G}; there is ζ such that each point has lifting invariant ζ ↦ [g_1]⋯[g_n]; and π_1(Conf^n A^1(C)) = B_n acts by σ_i(g) = (…, g_i g_{i+1} g_i^{−1}, g_i, …), so components ↔ B_n-orbits (Theorem 12.4, via Fried–Völklein). Corollary 12.6: the lifting invariant bijects the components of Y_C, and of Y_{F̄_q}, having a given 𝔖-invariant in 𝔖^{c,G}_{n,≥M} with the lifting invariants over it.
items.locator: Theorem 12.4, p. 49 (arXiv v2), and Corollary 12.6, pp. 49–50
items.note: The F̄_q half of Corollary 12.6 uses the specialization compatibility of Theorem 12.1 and the count of Lemma 10.3 on H^0.

items.name: Theorem 12.5: stable braid orbits are classified by the lifting invariant
items.statement: (Wood, Res. Math. Sci. 8 (2021), Theorem 3.1.) For finite G and c as in Notation 10.1 there is M such that (g_1, …, g_n) ↦ [g_1]⋯[g_n] maps c^{n,G}_{1,≥M} (generating tuples with product 1 in which every class of c/G occurs at least M times) onto K(G, c)_{n,≥M}, with fibers exactly the B_n-orbits.
items.locator: Theorem 12.5, p. 49 (arXiv v2), p. 49
items.note: A purely group-theoretic statement; PAPER-WOOD-19 routes the same stable braid-orbit classification (its item /134) to IG.3.

items.name: Proposition 12.7 and Corollary 12.9: counting Frobenius-fixed components
items.statement: For q prime to |G|, b(G,c,q,n) = Σ_{m ∈ ker(Z^{c/G}_{≡q,n,≥0} → G^ab)} nr_{q−1}(W_{q^{−1}}(m)) (nr_k(a) the number of k-th roots of a), π_{G,c}(q,n) = b(G,c,q,n) + O_G(n^{d_{G,c}(q)−2}), and b = 0 ⇒ π_{G,c}(q,n) = 0 (Proposition 12.7). For each a ∈ (Z/|G|²)^× there are M_a, a non-empty set E_a of residues and r_{a,b} > 0 with π_{G,c}(q,n) = 0 if n mod M_a ∉ E_a and = r_{a,b} n^{d_{G,c}(q)−1} + O_G(n^{d_{G,c}(q)−2}) if n ≡ b ∈ E_a, for q ≡ a mod |G|² (Corollary 12.9).
items.locator: Proposition 12.7, p. 50 (arXiv v2), and Corollary 12.9, pp. 50–53
items.note: π_{G,c}(q,n) is the number of Frobenius-fixed components of (𝓗ur^n_{G,c})_{F̄_q}, and d_{G,c}(q) the number of q-power orbits on the non-trivial classes in c. The component bound uses Ellenberg–Venkatesh Lemma 3.3.

items.name: Theorem 10.4: G-components versus Γ-components
items.statement: Let H be a finite admissible Γ-group, G = H⋊Γ and c as in Lemma 10.2. There is C_G > 0 and, for each a ∈ (Z/|G|²)^×, M_a and a non-empty set E_a of residues such that for all n and prime powers q ≡ a mod |G|² with gcd(q(q−1), |H|) = 1: π_{G,c}(q,n) = π_Γ(q,n) + O_G(n^{d_Γ(q)−2}); if n mod M_a ∉ E_a then π_{G,c}(q,n) = π_Γ(q,n) = 0; and if n mod M_a ∈ E_a and n is large, π_Γ(q,n) ≥ C_G n^{d_Γ(q)−1}.
items.locator: Theorem 10.4, p. 39 (arXiv v2), proof in §12, pp. 53–55
items.note: b(G,c,q,n) = b(Γ, Γ∖1, q, n), from Lemma 12.10, G^ab ≅ Γ^ab (H admissible), the bijection c/G ↔ (Γ∖1)/Γ, and a kernel of order prime to q−1.

items.name: Lemma 12.8: lattice points on a hyperplane in the positive orthant
items.statement: Let L ⊂ Z^d be a translate of a full lattice by an integer vector and a_i ≥ 0 integers, not all 0. There are k ≥ 1, a residue s mod k and r > 0 such that L′(n) = L ∩ {Σ a_i x_i = n} is empty unless n ≡ s mod k, and then #(L′(n) ∩ {x_i ≥ 0}) = r n^{d−1} + O_{d,L,a}(n^{d−2}).
items.locator: Lemma 12.8, p. 51 (arXiv v2)
items.note: An application of Davenport's principle (Lipschitz) after projecting away one coordinate.

items.name: Free profinite (pro-𝒞, pro-p) groups and pro-p presentations
items.statement: Free pro-|Γ|′ groups on finite sets, their pro-𝒞 completions, and minimal presentations of pro-p groups with generator and relation ranks d(G) = dim H¹(G, F_p), r(G) = dim H²(G, F_p) (NSW Corollary 3.9.3).
items.note: The upstream ProfiniteProPGroups roadmap plans free pro-p and pro-𝒞 groups on finite sets for a structured class 𝒞 (Layer 4; the prime-to-|Γ| groups form such a class) and presentations with rank interpretations (Layer 5).

items.name: Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula and Deligne's weight bound
items.statement: For a scheme Z over F_q, #Z(F_q) = Σ_j (−1)^j Tr(Frob | H^j_{c,ét}(Z_{F̄_q}, Q_ℓ)); for Z of dimension n the trace on H^{2n}_c is q^n times the number of Frobenius-fixed n-dimensional components; and every Frobenius eigenvalue on H^j_c has absolute value ≤ q^{j/2} (Deligne, Weil II, Théorème 1).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 1.4, p. 40
items.note: Following PAPER-WOOD-19: the trace formula for rational point counts is planned in SF.2 (integrating CohomologicalPointCounting), the top-degree trace on one component in EDC.2 (pairings), and Deligne's bound (H^i_c of weight ≤ i) in DWP.7.

items.name: Haar probability measure on compact groups; Carathéodory extension; Fatou and dominated convergence
items.statement: Haar measure on the compact group 𝓕_n (for random relations), Carathéodory extension of a countably additive premeasure from the algebra generated by basic opens, Fatou's lemma and dominated convergence.
items.locator: Definition 3.15 and §5, pp. 17, 29–30
items.note: Mathlib: MeasureTheory.Measure.haar and isHaarMeasure_haarMeasure (Measure/Haar/Basic.lean), MeasureTheory.AddContent.measure (OuterMeasure/OfAddContent.lean, Carathéodory extension of a σ-subadditive content), MeasureTheory.lintegral_liminf_le (Fatou) and MeasureTheory.tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence.

routes.reason: IG.4 owns embedding problems with local constraints. PAPER-WOOD-19 routes the analogous facts there (its 'No everywhere-unramified split-infinity extension of the base', the global lifting-invariant input and marked extensions). The Galois-side inputs of LWZB belong there too: the Γ-action on Gal(K^#/K) (Definition 2.1), admissibility of unramified Galois groups (Proposition 2.2), and Property E for Gal(K^#/K) via the central embedding problem and a global character (Theorem 2.5, Lemmas 2.6–2.7).

IG.5 owns Hurwitz moduli, braid/Nielsen components and tame reduction. PAPER-WOOD-19 already routes the marked Hurwitz scheme, its rational points, lifting-invariant components, specialization and the Betti comparison there, and PAPER-ELLENBERG-VENKATESH-WESTERLAND-16 routes its Hurwitz-space inputs to IG.3 and IG.5. LWZB's Hurwitz schemes 𝓗ur^n_{G,c}, the analytic and topological comparisons, the point and component counts (Lemmas 10.2–10.3, 11.8, Theorems 12.1, 12.4, Proposition 12.7, Corollaries 12.2, 12.6, 12.9) and the G-versus-Γ comparison (Theorem 10.4) are instances.

IG.3 owns the braid action on generating tuples with product one. PAPER-WOOD-19 routes the stable braid-orbit classification by the lifting invariant (its item /134) there, and LWZB's Theorem 12.5 quotes the same theorem.

ST.5 owns function-field analogues, higher moments and the measures on the limiting space. PAPER-WOOD-19 and PAPER-ELLENBERG-VENKATESH-WESTERLAND-16 route their function-field moment theorems there. LWZB's Theorem 1.4 and Corollary 1.5, with the counting dictionary of Lemmas 9.1 and 9.3, are the same kind of statement.

RS-07 narrows ST.2 to arithmetic-family counts and names GN.4 as the supplier of generic lattice-point estimates and Davenport counting, and PAPER-BHARGAVA-SHANKAR-WANG-25 routes Davenport's lemma to GN.4. Lemma 12.8 (lattice points of a translated lattice on a hyperplane in the positive orthant) is a generic count of this kind.

That lemma says: for H an admissible |Γ|′-Γ-group and G = H⋊Γ, there are Schur covers S → G and S_Γ → Γ compatible with G → Γ, and H_2(G, Z) → H_2(Γ, Z) has kernel of order prime to |Γ|. Import ordinary Schur covers and factor sets from the upstream Layer 7; do not rebuild them.

sourceIssues.printed: "… because N_p is a projective Z_p[Γ]-module (since Z_p[Γ] is hereditary) and N_p ⊗ Q_p ≅ (𝓕_n)^𝒞_p ⊗ Q_p (since N_p is a submodule of (𝓕_n)^𝒞_p ≅ (Z_p[Γ])^n of finite index and is torsion-free)."
sourceIssues.correction: (𝓕_n)^𝒞_p ≅ (Z_p[Γ]/(Σ_{g∈Γ} g))^n, the n-th power of the augmentation ideal.
sourceIssues.reason: For 𝒞 the abelian |Γ|′-Γ-groups, (𝓕_n)^𝒞 = 𝓕_n^ab, and Corollary 3.10 of the paper gives 𝓕_n^ab ≅ (Z[Γ]/(Σ_g g))^n with no Γ-invariants, whereas (Z_p[Γ])^n has invariants Z_p^n. The argument goes through unchanged: finite-index Γ-sublattices of a lattice over the hereditary order Z_p[Γ] are projective with the same rational span, hence isomorphic (Serre, Linear representations, §16, Theorem 34, Corollary 2).

Then µ_u(V_{C,H}) = …"; "Theorem 6.2. Let X_u be a random Γ-group with distribution µ_u. For any integer u …"
sourceIssues.correction: State Theorem 5.12 for every integer u. Its proof applies Lemma 5.10 to f_n(H, ℓ) = µ_{u,n}(U_{𝒞_ℓ,H}), g_n(H) = |Sur_Γ(𝓕_n, H)|/(|Aut_Γ(H)||Y(H)|^{n+u}) and g(H) = |Aut_Γ(H)|^{−1}|Y(H)|^{−u}. The inequality g_n ≤ g holds for every u, because |Sur_Γ(𝓕_n, H)| ≤ |Y(H)|^n by Corollary 3.8. Corollary 5.9 only needs u > −n, which holds for large n. So nothing in the argument uses u ≥ 0.
sourceIssues.reason: For u < 0, Theorems 5.15, 6.2 and 7.4–7.5 evaluate µ_u on Borel sets V_{𝒞,H} and integrate against µ_u. That requires µ_u to extend to a Borel measure, which is proved (Theorem 5.12, with Carathéodory extension) only for u ≥ 0 as printed. The main Theorems 1.2 and 1.4 use u = 1 and are unaffected. With the hypothesis dropped the statements hold. For example, at u = −1 and Γ = Z/2 the formula gives measure 0 to every finite abelianization, consistent with the free rank-one abelianization of 𝓕_n/(n−1 relations).
